$comment: Declarative table of agent configs `dotf deploy` installs (CLI-039, #1023).
One entry per config. The behaviour — plan, render, compare, install — is
the same for all of them, which is why it stopped being duplicated across
setup-linux.sh and setup-windows.ps1 (ADR-020 C7: shell keeps the thin
bootstrap, Go owns tooling logic).
Fields:
name      the argument to `dotf deploy <name>`
src       repo-relative source
dst       destination; {VAR} resolves through `dotf env` (ADR-025), {HOME} is
the user's home. An unresolvable token is an error, never an empty
path segment.
render    run `dotf secrets render` on the staged copy before installing
mode      octal permissions. DECLARED, never inferred: guessing which configs
hold credentials is the guess that already went wrong in #987.
strategy  replace (default): the source becomes the whole destination.
merge: the source is written into the destination's JSON object,
or TOML table when the destination ends in .toml (#2013 H4), and
every key the source does not name is preserved, for a file
the reading tool also writes (AI-039, #1322). Objects merge
recursively and lists union, so an entry the tool added at runtime
inside a managed key survives too (AI-042); a managed scalar is the
repo's, and `dotf deploy <name>` puts it back when the tool
changed it. In sync means the merge would change nothing.
requires  a command that must be on PATH for the entry to apply; absent,
the entry is skipped and reported. A config for a tool the box
does not carry is a file nobody reads (#843), and the integration
guard asserts ~/.copilot never appears without copilot (#1312).
paths     native | slash: render the {VAR} tokens found inside the source's
JSON string values (the same tokens dst uses) and write each such
string with the OS separator (native) or with / (slash), before
the strategy runs. Which form a tool accepts is a measured fact
about the tool: Copilot wrote backslash trustedFolders into its own
config on Windows; agy has read C:/... trustedWorkspaces there daily.
Declare the observed form, never guess (AI-042, #1334).
platforms the GOOS values (linux, darwin, windows) the entry applies on;
absent means every OS, and an OS not listed is skipped, not
failed - the meaning packages.json gives it. Needs version 4: the
dotf that reads 4 also reads 3, so this file moves to 4 with its
first OS-only entry, once the release carrying that reader is the
DOTF_VERSION pin (#1843 B1).
version 3 (AI-042): paths changes what an entry's CONTENT means. Version 2
(AI-039): strategy and requires change what an entry MEANS, so a
dotf that predates them refuses this file instead of deploying every entry
as replace - which would overwrite ~/.copilot/settings.json and wipe the box's
own keys. Bump it again whenever a new field changes meaning: a field an old
decoder does not know is invisible to it, the version is not.
Copilot's destinations are spelled {HOME}/.copilot rather than {COPILOT_HOME}:
`dotf deploy` runs before `dotf env set`/`generate` in both setups, so on a
first run machine.json — which {COPILOT_HOME} needs to resolve — does not
exist yet. The contract's default for COPILOT_HOME is this very path.
opencode.jsonc is deliberately absent: it is gated on testing whether opencode
resolves {env:VAR} itself rather than assuming it, which is the assumption that
made #987 expensive (#1843 B12). Its tui.json carries no secrets and is here.
Claude's MCP servers and plugins are not files, so they are converge steps of
a bare `dotf deploy`, not entries here (CLI-063, #1339).
claude-settings merges ai/claude/settings.json into the settings.json Claude
Code reads, under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (the contract default is ~/.claude). Every
template key is written, so the template IS the list of what dotfiles owns:
it must never carry `hooks`, which `dotf harness bind` owns (HARNESS-045).
pi-compaction merges ONLY the compaction key into pi's settings.json, a file
pi rewrites at runtime. The rest of that file is seeded once by the setup
scripts, which run the seed BEFORE `dotf deploy`: the other order lets this
merge create a settings.json holding nothing but compaction, and the seed then
sees a file and never writes defaultProvider/defaultModel (#1938). reserveTokens
is round(0.6 x contextWindow) from ai/pi/models.json, so compaction triggers at
40% of the window; tests/pi-config.bats derives and asserts every value.
docker-config merges cliPluginsExtraDirs into ~/.docker/config.json so the
docker CLI finds the compose and buildx plugins Homebrew installs under
/opt/homebrew/lib/docker/cli-plugins, a directory outside its default search
path (#2013 P5b). It requires colima, which only the brew catalog entry
provisions, so it applies on the Mac and skips elsewhere without needing
`platforms`. Merge keeps what docker and colima write there (auths,
currentContext); mode 0600 because auths can hold registry credentials.
